response.sql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT s.scancount, s.gbsize, s.spanmin, si.healtheval
  FROM scans s
  JOIN sites si ON si.zoneregistry = s.zoneref
  WHERE s.chronotag >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274'
    AND s.chronotag <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797'
    AND si.healtheval IS NOT NULL
),
by_status AS (
  SELECT healtheval AS status,
         SUM(scancount) AS total_scans,
         AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_min
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY healtheval
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_min) AS mean_of_status_avgs FROM by_status
)
SELECT b.status,
       b.total_scans,
       b.avg_gb_per_min,
       b.avg_gb_per_min - o.mean_of_status_avgs AS deviation_from_mean
FROM by_status b
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.mean_of_status_avgs IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: chronotag is compared as text using the given bounds, as the request specifies. This only matches chronological order if every stored value uses the same 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' layout. The documentation says the column is a TIMESTAMP and may hold Excel serial numbers, and those values would not compare correctly as text.
Scans are linked to sites by scans.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry. Scans whose site has a NULL healtheval are excluded, since they have no health and safety status to group by.

The per-status average is the mean of the per-scan ratio gbsize / spanmin. Rows with a NULL gbsize or spanmin are ignored. A spanmin of 0 is treated as missing via NULLIF to avoid division by zero. The 'mean of all status-level averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-status averages, and no rows are returned if that mean is NULL.
